Unlike standard ray marching which samples every voxel, this method skips low-intensity regions by only processing nodes whose maximum stored value exceeds the current global maximum found along the ray [S1].

The evidence describes a method using a priority queue and min/max multilevel grids. It states that the algorithm iteratively takes the node with the highest max value and terminates if a leaf cell appears at the head of the priority queue. This implies that nodes with lower maximum values (which would not be at the head or would be processed later/ignored if a higher value leaf is found) are effectively skipped or not processed for the final result, aligning with the claim that it skips low-intensity regions by only processing nodes whose maximum stored value exceeds the current global maximum (represented by the head of the priority queue).
